items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Elvin says, “Let’s do it!” So I do it because we don’t have piano at that time and he did the music then Jimmy started playing bass in our apartment.

ctx.x: I’m holding in my hand a copy of “Poly Curtains” and this date is September 26th, a little after your birthday of that year in 1969 and this one has a composition entitled “Mr. Jones” this one has Joe Farrell and also George Coleman and Wilbur Little on bass and Condita on congas. This happened to be a particular favorite of mine. I just wanted to ask Keiko about “Mr. Jones” since that happen to be one of my favorites.

Yeah. Before that I wrote a tune “Shinjitsu” Truth. Because when I come to start a living over there with that man, a shock. Culture shock. So I wanted to give him, because it was during a time when I trust everyone. For example everyone say, “I call you Keiko” because I don’t know how to do the booking business, I have no friends. Then people say “Oh okay I have a job I call you” and I am excited. So I wait 24 hours. Elvin say, “Go out. Are you crazy?” I say, “No I cannot go out because they are going to call” I…
That was quite an album cover, you know Georgia. That’s probably current. The “Mr. Jones” album, it’s like silhouette of a Dandy with a tuxedo on.
